name: Ce Deng
description: Ce Deng (æ–œé’‰) is a Chinese domino game where tiles are laid with adjacent ends matching, similar to Western domino layout. Uses Chinese domino set (32 tiles; 21 unique, 11 duplicated). Best for four players; winner has fewest pips on discarded and unplayed tiles.

history.origins: China. Ce Deng (æ–œé’‰): domino matching game; tiles laid with adjacent ends matching. Chinese set 32 tiles.

setup.dealing: Four players receive eight tiles each. With fewer players, eight tiles each are often used; remainder unused. First player in the first deal is random; thereafter the winner of each deal leads the next.
setup.equipment: Chinese domino set or domino cards.

rules.objective: On your turn, play a tile that matches the single open end of the layout and call the new open end, or if unable, discard one tile face down and say drink. The player with fewest pips on discarded and unplayed tiles wins the deal and leads the next. Pairs settle by pip difference.
rules.gameplay: First player leads any tile and declares which end is open. Play is clockwise or counter-clockwise (alternates by deal). Each turn: play a matching tile and call the new open end, or discard one tile face down and call drink. If three players drink in succession, the last player who played plays again. If no one can match, the game is blocked and ends; count unplayed tiles as well.
keyRules: Single open end; match or discard
Pass, head seven, tail eight double payments

strategy.basic: Discard high-pip tiles when you must drink; keep a variety of halves in hand to maximize the chance of matching when it is your turn.
strategy.intermediate: Play defensively. Lead high tiles like 6-6 or 6-5 to force others to discard; try to monopolize a short half such as 2.
strategy.advanced: The 2 half has only seven tiles total; attack by leading 5-2 and declaring 2 open, then playing 2-2 to force another round of discards. Coordinate with another player to duo-polize short suits.
tips: Keep variety of halves so you can match when the turn returns.
Settle per pair by pip difference; stake per pip agreed in advance.
